a. It is the policy of the City of Griffin, Georgia, pursuant to the federal Fair Housing Act Amendments of 1988, 42 U.S.C. § 3601 et seq. (hereafter "FHAA") and Title II of the Americans With Disabilities Act (hereafter "ADA", or collectively the "fair housing laws") to provide individuals with disabilities reasonable accommodation in its rules, regulations, standards, policies, practices, and procedures pertaining to housing and development to ensure equal access by persons with disabilities and to developers of housing for persons with disabilities. This section establishes a procedure for making requests for reasonable accommodation in land use, zoning, and development regulations as found and contained in this Code. It is the intent of the City of Griffin, its officers, staff, and agents to fully comply with the intent and purpose of fair housing laws.
b. Reasonable accommodation in the land use, zoning, and development context means providing individuals with disabilities or developers of housing for people with disabilities, flexibility in the application of land use, zoning, and building regulations, policies, standards, practices, and procedures, or even waiving certain requirements altogether, when it is necessary to eliminate legal and regulatory barriers to housing opportunities.
1. For purposes of this section, an individual with a disability is someone who has a physical or mental impairment that limits one or more major life activities; anyone who is regarded as having such impairment; or anyone with a history of such impairment. The terms "disability" and "handicap", for purposes of the fair housing laws have the same meaning.
2. A request for a reasonable accommodation may be made by any individual with a disability, his or her representative, or a developer or provider of housing for individuals with disabilities, when the application of a land use, zoning, or development regulation, policy, standard, practice, or procedure acts as a barrier to fair housing opportunities. Development regulations shall mean those minimum standards set forth in this Unified Development Code and shall not include Georgia Statewide Minimum Building Codes, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 8-2-20, or environmental regulations found in general law or the Code of Griffin, Georgia.
c. Notice of the availability of reasonable accommodation shall be prominently displayed on the official bulletin board (2d Floor, E. Solomon Street entrance to One Griffin Center), the city's website, and at the permit counter in the Development Services Office (3d Floor, One Griffin Center). Such notice shall state where applications for requesting reasonable accommodation are available to the public.
d. Any eligible person described in (b)(2) above may request a reasonable accommodation in the application of any land use, zoning, or development regulation, rule, standard, policy, standard, practice, or procedure as described in subsection (b)(2) above, by completing and filing an application requesting reasonable accommodation with the director of development services, in triplicate. Persons requesting reasonable accommodation are encouraged to consult the director prior to submitting the application in order to make the nature of and need for the request clear.
1. All requests shall be made in writing, on forms provided by the city, and provide the following information:
A. Name, address, and telephone number of person filing the request. When available, an email address should also be provided. When the request is being filed for the benefit of an individual with disabilities, the name, address, and telephone number for that person shall also be stated.
B. Address of property; name, address and telephone number of property owner, if different from requestor.
C. Detailed description of the requested accommodation and the regulation, rule, standard, policy, practice, or procedure for which accommodation is sought; and
D. Reason that accommodation is sought and any supporting documentation. If medical information is provided to support a determination that the requestor is a person with disabilities, it should be clearly marked as "Confidential" and will be used only as needed.
2. Any information identified by the applicant as confidential will be held and used by the city in such manner as to respect the individual's privacy rights and shall not be made available for public inspection.
3. A request for reasonable accommodation may be filed at any time; however, the city encourages its filing at the earliest opportunity to ensure the applicant with equal access to housing and to allow the city to make timely determinations of other related pending applications and permits. City staff will afford the applicant, upon request, such assistance as needed to ensure the application process is accessible and meaningful. There shall be no fee for requesting a reasonable accommodation.
4. Granting of a reasonable accommodation does not affect an individual's obligations to comply with other applicable regulations not at issue in the requested accommodation.
e. All requests for reasonable accommodation shall be reviewed by a committee, consisting of the chairperson, city manager, and development services director. A written decision on the request shall be issued to the applicant within ten business days of the receipt of a completed form (Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays excluded). After initial review of a request, the committee may request additional information from the applicant.
f. The written decision to grant, deny, or grant upon conditions a request shall be consistent with the fair housing laws and based upon the following factors:
1. Whether the housing, which is the subject of the request for reasonable accommodation, will be used by an individual(s) with disabilities protected by the fair housing laws;
2. Whether the requested accommodation is necessary to make housing available to an individual with disabilities protected under the fair housing laws;
3. Whether the requested accommodation would impose an undue financial or administrative burden on the city; and
4. Whether the requested accommodation would require a fundamental alteration of a material nature in the city's land use, zoning, or development policies.
Where the written decision is to deny the request, or grant the request subject to conditions, a sufficiently detailed explanation of the reasons shall be given the applicant. The decision of the review committee shall be final and binding upon the city. Notice of the decision shall be given the applicant by Certified U.S. Mail, return receipt requested, unless the applicant consents to service in a different manner.
g. While a request for reasonable accommodation is pending, all laws, rules, regulations, standards, policies, practices, and procedures applicable to the property that is the subject of the request shall remain in full force and effect. This shall include any appeal of the decision until final.
h. Within 30 days of an adverse decision on a request for reasonable accommodation, an aggrieved person may file a Petition for Writ of Certiorari in the Superior Court of Spalding County, Georgia. Nothing in this procedure shall preclude an aggrieved person from seeking other available federal or state remedies.

(1) Purpose and intent. Throughout this Code, provisions are made for the issuance by the city of various licenses, permits, and approvals. Some are required by federal or state law while others are part of a comprehensive regulatory scheme adopted by the board of commissioners. The commission finds that the number of ever-increasing demands on city staff, resources, and infrastructure is limited, not only by budgetary constraints, but physical limitations and manpower. It is the objective of this commission to utilize its resources wisely, fairly, and in the most efficient manner, while requiring consideration of criteria and standards without discrimination or favor. The intent of this section is to recognize and provide guidance for city staff and this commission as the city's governing authority to ensure that city services, privileges, and benefits are delivered in a non-discriminatory manner.
Most all forms of licenses, permits, and approvals required by the city involve some form of deployment of city resources. In order to conserve and allocate these resources wisely, the city often must balance competing factors affecting its citizens, property owners, residents and businesses. Licensing and permitting often requires some form of due process, or notice, and can only be approved following a hearing or other means of allowing citizens to be heard. Adequate advance notice to the pertinent city staff is key to timely and relevant decision-making, as well as a full understanding of material facts and the applicant's objectives. Normally, the burden is on the applicant to apprise the city staff of material information by filing a complete application.
Fees charged in relation to permits or licenses are established to recoup the city's cost of permit/license review and administration. In certain cases, the fee will also seek to recoup anticipated costs to the city for the burden placed on infrastructure and services, such as additional security and traffic control. The upfront payment of required fees is part of the submission of a complete application. Waiver or reduction of fees and waiver of a complete written application is discouraged, except as incentives for economic development, and should only be approved by the city manager, upon written recommendation of a department manager.
Last, while it is the general intent of this commission to make its permitting and licensing procedures as simplified as possible, the need for fully informed decision-making by city staff and this commission mandates the need for consistency and transparency, which are only attainable through a written application process, followed by documented verification and review. In all instances where applications are filed, the city will seek to provide a timely response to the applicant, with all final decisions (approval, denial, or approval upon reasonable conditions) given to the applicant in writing.
(2) Non-discrimination. This provision shall apply to all licensing, permitting, and/or approval requests found in this Code. Though certain Code sections may contain objective criteria or standards relevant to the specific license, permit, or approval sought, this provision shall serve as an overlay and guide the decision-making process.
i. No license, permit, or approval shall be denied nor shall the applicant be given less favorable treatment as to time, place, or manner requirements or conditions on account of the race, color, creed, religion, gender, domestic relationship status, familial status, sexual orientation, national origin, political affiliation, or gender identity of the applicant and/or participants in the business, undertaking, event, or activity to be carried out by the applicant under such license, permit, or approval.
ii. No license, permit, or approval shall be denied nor shall the applicant be given less favorable treatment as to time, place, or manner requirements or conditions based upon the message or content of speech of the applicant and/or participants in the business, undertaking, event, or activity to be carried out by the applicant under such license, permit, or approval.
iii. Where it is assumed or reasonably believed that issuance of a license, permit, or approval is likely to result in unreasonable hostility by opponents of an applicant and/or its group or entity, or there is a heighten risk to public safety, based upon the content of speech or the message conveyed by the applicant and/or participants in the undertaking, event, or activity to be carried out by the applicant under such license, permit, or approval, reasonable accommodation as to time, place, and manner requirements shall be afforded, including provision of city resources necessary for traffic control, and police and fire protection; provided, however, payment for or reimbursement of the cost of such accommodation may be imposed by the city as a reasonable condition for such approval.
iv. All other conditions or modifications of the time, place, and manner requirements for a license, permit, or approval shall be reasonable and imposed based upon compelling reasons relating to public safety, health, or the environment. When approval is based upon the imposition of reasonable conditions, all such conditions shall be clearly set forth in the written notice of decision.

b. Matter presented. The mayor will announce the proposed zoning action request in the order set forth on the agenda published in accordance with Open Meetings Law and shall state that printed copies of the adopted standards governing the exercise of the zoning power, factors for consideration, and procedures governing the hearing are available to the public. The city manager's designee shall advise the commission of the nature of the decision sought and the recommendations of the planning and zoning board and city staff, including any conditions, prior to receiving public input on the proposed zoning decision.
c. Speakers. Following presentation by the city manager's designee as provided in subsection (1)(b) of this section, the mayor shall call each person who has signed up to speak in favor of the proposed zoning decision, starting with the applicant or his representative and followed by the other proponents of the action, if any, until the maximum time for proponent presentation has been reached as provided in subsection (1)(d) of this section. After all proponent speakers have addressed the board of commissioners, or after the maximum time for proponents has been reached, whichever comes first, the mayor shall call each person who has signed up to speak in opposition to the proposed zoning decision in the order in which they signed up, subject to the time limitations set forth in subsection (1)(d) of this section. Only those persons who signed up to speak prior to the commencement of the hearing shall be entitled to speak, unless the mayor, in his discretion, allows the person to speak to the zoning decision, notwithstanding the failure of the person to sign up prior to the hearing.
d. Time limits. Proponents, including the applicant or his attorney/representative, shall have no less than ten minutes for presentation of data, evidence and expert opinions, provided that the applicant is entitled to utilize the entirety of this minimum time and may reserve time for rebuttal; likewise, opponents of the proposed decision shall have no less than ten minutes for presentation of data, evidence and expert opinion in support of their position. (1) Applicability.
a. This section shall not apply to zoning decisions for the rezoning of property from a single-family residential use of property to a multifamily residential use of property when the rezoning is initiated by the owner or authorized agent of the owner of such property or when the local government adopts a zoning ordinance or zoning map applicable to the entire land area under the governance of the local government, as opposed to a subset of parcels of land under the governance of the local government.
b. Notwithstanding any other provisions of this Article to the contrary, when a proposed zoning decision relates to an amendment of the zoning ordinance to revise one or more zoning classifications or definitions related to single-family residential uses of property so as to authorize multifamily uses of property pursuant to such classification or definitions, or to grant permission under certain or all circumstances, for property owners to deviate from the existing zoning requirements of a single-family residential zoning, such zoning decision shall be adopted in the manner set forth in subsection (b) of this section.
(2) Special procedure.
a. The zoning decision shall be adopted at two regular meetings of the local government making the zoning decisions, during a period of at least 15 but not more than 45 days apart; and
b. Prior to the first meeting provided for in subparagraph (1) of this paragraph, at least two public hearings shall be held on the proposed action. Such public hearings shall be held at least three months and not more than nine months prior to the date of final action on the zoning decisions. Furthermore, at least one of the public hearings shall be held between the hours of 5:00 p.m. and 8:00 p.m. The hearings required by this paragraph shall be in addition to any hearing required under Section 408B.
c. The local government shall give notice of such hearing by:
i. Posting notice on each affected premises in the manner prescribed in Section 408D; provided, however, that when more than 500 parcels are affected, in which case posting notice is required every 500 feet in the affected area; and
ii. Publishing in a newspaper of general circulation within the territorial boundaries of the local government a notice of each hearing at least 15 days and not more than 45 days prior to the date of the hearing.
d. Both the posted notice and published notice provided in subsection (b)(3) of this section shall include a prominent statement that the proposed zoning decision relates to or will authorize multifamily uses or give permission to the property owner to deviate from the zoning requirements of a single-family residential zoning of property in classification previously relating to single-family residential uses. The published notice shall be at least nine column inches in size and shall not be located in the classified advertising section of the newspaper. e. All public hearings related to zoning decisions to which this section is applicable shall be conducted pursuant to the hearing procedures set forth in Section 408E(1).

113:
1. If either a use or class of use is not specifically indicated as being permitted in a zoning district, either as a matter of right or as a special use, then, such use, class of use, or structures for such uses, shall be prohibited in such district.
Uses that are not specifically indicated but clearly resemble other permitted uses may be considered by director upon written request for review. Determination of whether such use clearly resembles other permitted uses shall be made based on (1) uses that share the same subcategory classification code in the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) or other standardized coding for businesses and (2) whether the proposed use generates equal or less traffic or nuisance than similar uses which are indicated as permitted.
115:
A data center is an industrial use involving a building, facility, campus of facilities, or array of interconnected buildings or facilities which exists for the principal purpose of housing, cooling, and securing working data servers and is developed for the storage, management, processing, and transmission of digital data associated with technological equipment, applications, systems, and services. This section shall not apply to institutional use facilities for which the storage, management, processing, and transmission of digital data occurring on the premises is incidental to the principal business purpose, provided that the room or building housing the data servers is less than 2,000 square feet and does not have a substation.
While data centers provide necessary infrastructure for the modern world, this land use generally requires significant land, energy, and water consumption that can have a detrimental impact on the community. Further, the uses can generate higher levels of truck traffic, noise, vibration, and other conditions that may not be compatible with nearby uses. These requirements are intended to ensure the promotion and protection of the community's health, safety, and welfare through supplemental regulation of data centers as an industrial use while balancing economic development and the modern need for data infrastructure.
Only data centers meeting the definition of either a minor data center or major data center are permitted within the jurisdictional limits of the City of Griffin. All data centers shall require issuance of a special use permit and must conform to the following requirements:
(1) Types of data centers permitted by special use.
(a) Minor data center. A data center comprised of a single principal building with an area up to 10,000 square feet that does not have a substation. Minor data centers are permitted on parcels zoned Planned Industrial Development (PID) by special use permit, subject to requirements of Section 503A.
(b) Major data center. A data center comprised of a single principal building with an area greater than 10,000 square feet and not more than 275,000 square feet that may have a substation. Major data centers are permitted on parcels zoned Planned Industrial Development (PID) by special use permit, subject to requirements of Section 503A.
(2) Site planning and building design.
(a) Minimum acreage.
(i) Minor data center: Minimum 5 acres.
(ii) Major data center: Minimum 10 acres.
(b) Lot dimensions.
(i) Lot coverage (impervious surface): Maximum 70%.
(c) Setbacks. Primary operational facilities and infrastructure, including the principal data center building housing active servers, electrical substations, emergency generators, and mechanical systems must be located in a manner that complies with the following:
(i) Minor data center.
(A) 200 feet from any public right-of-way;
(B) 200 feet from any nonresidential use or zoning district; and
(C) 1,000 feet from any residential dwelling.
(ii) Major data center.
(A) 200 feet from any public right-of-way;
(B) 500 feet from any nonresidential use or district; and
(C) 1,500 feet from any residential dwelling.
(iii) Accessory structures that do not generate noise or emission may be allowed in a setback subject to development review approval. No such structure may be located within a required buffer.
(d) Buffers. Final buffer design must be provided to the city at the time of the application for special use. All data centers must preserve at least 30 percent of the gross lot area as natural, undisturbed open space. Buffers, stormwater features, and passive recreation areas may be utilized to satisfy the requirement, subject to development review approval. Established undisturbed natural buffers shall be retained. Planted buffer must consist of 50 percent evergreen and trees must be at least six feet within two years of planting. An undisturbed or enhanced landscape buffer complying with the following requirements must be required along all property lines, except when adjacent to an industrial use or zoning district:
(i) Minor data center: 100 feet in width.
(ii) Major data center: 200 feet in width.
(e) Building configuration.
(i) If adjoining a non-residential use or zoning district, maximum building height: 50 feet.
(ii) If adjoining a residential use or zoning district, maximum building height: 40 feet.
(iii) If above 35 feet, a fire control plan must be approved by the fire chief or designee during development review.
(f) Architectural controls.
(i) Prohibited exterior materials:
(A) Gray concrete block
(ii) Exterior materials (visible from public right-of-way):
(A) Solid wood
(B) Decorative concrete block
(C) Stucco
(D) Corrugated metal
(E) Hardy plank
(F) Brick
(G) Glass
(iii) Air conditioning, HVAC systems, and generators must be thoroughly screened from view from the public right-of-way and adjacent properties by using walls, fencing, roof elements, or landscaping, and shall be located not less than 100 feet from adjacent property lines.
(g) Accessory structures. Accessory structures are prohibited in front of the principal structure or in the front yard. The structure must be no larger than 25 percent of the principal structure's floor area and must be finished using approved exterior materials listed above in subsection (2)(f)(ii).
(h) Parking. No parking within the front, side, or rear yard setbacks.
(i) Storage. Outside storage is not permitted unless it is screened from view from adjoining streets and lots by wall or fence at least eight feet in height.
(j) Other physical requirements. The layout and orientation of buildings and associated equipment must minimize the visual impact on surrounding properties. Other more specific physical requirements related to architectural standards, buffers, accessory structures, parking, storage, screening, perimeter fencing, landscaping, security, or other similar regulations may be imposed as a condition of special use approval or may be imposed as part of the required development agreement between the city and the developer based on environmental impact, including noise and lighting, utility infrastructure requirements, and similar site-specific and use-specific needs assessments as necessary to prevent nuisance conditions and promote health, safety, and welfare.
(3) Development agreement:
(a) Prior to issuance of a land disturbance permit, a development agreement must be executed between the developer and the city. The development agreement may provide vested rights to the property owner during the term of the agreement to ensure that the development proceeds in compliance with land use regulations in effect on the date of the agreement. Development agreements must contain the following information:
(i) The time period and specific expiration date of the agreement and a time period and specific expiration date for development phases (if applicable);
(ii) Specifications of land uses, including population, density of development, and dimensions of buildings, lots, and site features, as applicable;
(iii) Description of public facilities and infrastructure to serve the development, including identification of all service providers and the time of service availability;
(iv) Description of easements that are necessary for public facilities and infrastructure;
(v) Identification of land to be reserved or dedicated for public purposes (if any);
(vi) Identification of land that is required to be protected;
(vii) Identification of development and building periods that are required, including a statement that failure to list a required permit would not relieve the property owner from compliance with all permitting requirements;
(viii) Identification of any conditions, terms, restrictions, or other requirements that may be necessary to protect the public health, safety, or welfare; and
(ix) Identification of all parties to the agreement.
(b) In addition to the required information set forth in subsection (a) above, the following areas of inquiry, at a minimum, must be considered in the development agreement; provided, however, that in the context of minor data centers, this requirement may be satisfied if both parties affirm and agree, as part of the agreement, that a particular subject was considered and based on evidence of minimal impact posed by the project:
(i) Compliance with the maximum noise limits set forth in this section and the most current City of Griffin Noise Control Ordinance, including during construction, normal operations, and testing activities. The city may require that on-site noise monitoring equipment be installed and maintained as part of the agreement;
(ii) Power and energy efficiency reporting;
(iii) The establishment of performance metrics to limit potable water consumption through the use of a closed loop or similar system designed to minimize consumption and eliminate continuous discharge or evaporative loss;
(iv) Ongoing metering of energy and water usage and transparency of grid impact during operations;
(v) Decommissioning, change of use, and site restoration;
(vi) Financial assurances such as performance bonds, security bonds, decommissioning bonds, or escrow accounts sufficient to ensure site restoration, infrastructure removal, environmental remediation, and long-term compliance with approved operational standards;
(vii) Ongoing assessment of facility impact on surrounding air and water quality during operations, including transparency of results and effective remediation of negative impacts if identified;
(viii) Emergency coordination with fire, police, and utility providers;
(ix) Environmental Impact Summary and Operations Management Plan, including potential third-party environmental impact study evaluating air, water, noise, and operational impacts;
(x) Documentation of coordination with electric and water utility providers, including evaluation of infrastructure capacity, required upgrades (if any), and cost allocation measures, demonstrating that project-related system improvements and service demands are borne by the applicant and not shifted to existing customers, with mitigation strategies incorporated into the development agreement;
(xi) Emergency generator testing and operational protocols consistent with the special use regulations, including testing schedules, duration, and noise mitigation measures, to ensure minimal impact on surrounding properties;
(xii) Impact on traffic during the construction phase and solutions to mitigate the impact;
(xiii) Requirements for parking during construction and after construction above what is required in the underlying zoning district;
(xiv) How the project may contribute development of inclusive, accessible, and mixed-use community surrounding the project via community benefits packaging, infrastructure upgrades, and reinvestment strategies; and
(xv) The use, storage, and management of batteries, fuels, backup power systems, or any hazardous materials associated with facility operations, including compliance with all fire marshal, EMA, and applicable life safety requirements.
(c) The following plans and studies shall be requested and reviewed when drafting and negotiating development agreements for data centers, provided that the city may request and consider any other plans or studies that it deems necessary in order to ensure protection of public health safety and welfare:
(i) Minor data center:
(A) Noise impact assessment
(B) Water consumption & sustainability plan
(C) Energy consumption & sustainability plan
(D) Lighting plan
(E) Stormwater management plan
(F) Sewer plan
(ii) Major data center:
(A) Noise impact assessment
(B) Water consumption & sustainability plan
(C) Energy consumption & sustainability plan
(D) Lighting plan
(E) Transmission line impact assessment
(F) Tree preservation & reforestation plan
(G) Stormwater management plan
(H) Sewer plan
(d) All development agreements must be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, Spalding County, Georgia.
(4) Lighting.
(a) Exterior illumination shall be designed to maintain the existing night sky darkness and to prevent light trespass onto adjacent properties. Illumination levels shall be measured from any height and orientation of the measuring device at any location along the property line, except the lighting of parking lots must be measured at grade with the meter sensor held horizontally at the surface. In order to obtain that objective, the following criteria (at a minimum) shall be met:
(i) All outdoor lighting fixtures shall be full cut-off type fixtures.
(ii) Outdoor lighting fixtures must be located, aimed or shielded to minimize glare and stray light trespassing across lot lines and into the public right-of-way;
(iii) Flood or spot lamps must be positioned no higher than 45 degrees above straight down (half-way between the vertical and the horizontal) when the source is visible from any off-site residential property or public roadway.
(iv) Light poles shall be no taller than 25 feet in height.
(v) All light poles must be setback a minimum of ten feet from any exterior property line.
(vi) Color temperature of outdoor lighting fixtures must not exceed 3000K at the light source.
(vii) Maximum foot-candles at property lines, including rights-of-way:
(A) At property line abutting a residential use: 0.5.
(B) At property line abutting an office or institutional use: 1.0.
(C) At property line abutting a commercial or industrial use: 1.5.
(viii) Foot-candles on off-street parking lots:
(A) Minimum footcandles: 1.0.
(B) Average footcandles: 5.0.
(C) Maximum footcandles: 8.0.
(ix) Security lighting must be directed towards the targeted area. Sensor activated lighting must be located in such a manner as to prevent direct glare and lighting into properties of others or into a public right-of-way, and the system must be designed and maintained so that lights are not activated by activity off of the subject property.
(x) All lighting fixtures servicing parking lots must be directed downward and not towards buildings or other areas. Parking must be illuminated to a minimum illumination level of 0.4 footcandles at grade level, and the ratio of the average illumination to the minimum illumination may not exceed 4:1. Light poles used in parking lots with 100 parking spaces or less may not exceed 20 feet in height. Light poles in parking lots with more than 100 parking spaces may not exceed 35 feet in height.
(b) A conceptual lighting plan must be submitted with the initial application sufficient to demonstrate conformity with these requirements. A complete lighting plan shall be submitted as part of the development review process showing conformity with these requirements, and any additional requirements imposed as a condition of the special use or as part of the development agreement between the applicant and the city. The required plans, descriptions, data, and supporting evidence of the same must be complete and accurate so that the planning and development department is able to readily determine whether the proposal will comply with the requirements of this section. The city requires the following information within the plan:
(i) The location on the premises of each outdoor illuminating device, both proposed and any already existing on the site;
(ii) A description of all proposed illumination devices, fixtures, lamps, supports, and reflectors. The description may include, but is not limited to, catalog cuts and illustrations by manufacturers.
(iii) Photometric data, such as that furnished by manufacturers or similar, showing the angle of cut-off of light emissions and the color temperature of all proposed illuminating devices, fixtures, lamps, supports, and reflectors.
(iv) Photometric plans must include the maximum and average light layout.
(c) Additional dark sky requirements or similar lighting regulations, including but not limited to security lighting, building mounted lighting, and perimeter illumination, may be imposed as a condition of special use approval or may be imposed as part of the required development agreement between the city and the applicant based on the specific use and site plan, environmental impact, utility infrastructure requirements, and similar site-specific and use-specific needs assessments as necessary to prevent nuisance conditions and promote health, safety, and welfare.
(5) Noise.
(a) Once the data center is operational, the maximum noise output at any property line adjacent to a residential district or use is 55 dBA between the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. At all other times, the maximum noise output is 45 dBA.
(b) Testing of generators or other equipment is only allowed during the hours of 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. On-site generator testing shall not take place for more than two hours per day. Testing is not allowed on any holiday recognized by the City of Griffin Board of Commissioners.
(c) With the exception of testing activities, generator use is limited to temporary or emergency backup use only. Use as prime power, rate curtailment, and storm avoidance shall not constitute a valid temporary or emergency backup use.
(d) An acoustic barrier (e.g. an exterior solid or louvered wall containing soundproofing materials) shall surround all exterior mechanical equipment, whether located on a roof top, on ground level, or elsewhere on the exterior of the property where necessary to achieve the sound level requirements above. The design, materials, height, and effectiveness of acoustical barriers are subject to development review and approval by the city. Such acoustic barrier must be shown on the approved site plan and shall be maintained on the premises of the data center for the operational life of the facility.
(e) Noise generated on the site during construction and/or development, prior to issuance of the certificate of occupancy or certificate of completion, as applicable, shall be governed by Chapter 42 (Environment), Article V (Noise Control), Code of Griffin.
(f) Additional regulations intended to mitigate the noise caused by data center operations may be imposed as a condition of special use approval or may be imposed as part of the required development agreement between the city and the applicant based on the specific use and site plan, adjacent property uses, noise impact assessments, and similar site-specific and use-specific needs assessments as necessary to prevent nuisance conditions and promote health, safety, and welfare.
(6) Water and sewer
(a) Data centers shall be served by the public water and sewer system. The development shall not utilize wells to provide water for any purpose.
(b) Open evaporative cooling systems are prohibited.
(c) Prior to the issuance of a land disturbance permit for a data center, the applicant shall submit to the city an analysis of raw water needs, including, at a minimum, the quantity of water required. The applicant must request and receive a letter indicating sufficient water and sewer capacity to serve the proposed data center.
(d) The city may require the developer to fund and implement all necessary water and/or sewer improvements necessitated by its use, as well as provide for monitoring, reporting, and enforcement to ensure long-term sustainability of water and infrastructure resources.
(e) Applicants shall provide, at a minimum, the following plans and studies related to water and sewer, provided that the city may request other plans or studies as necessary to evaluate the impact on public health, safety, and welfare:
(i) Water consumption & sustainability plan.
(ii) Sewer plan.
(f) Additional water and sewer regulations may be imposed as a condition of special use approval or as part of the required development agreement between the city and the applicant based on the specific use and site plan, environmental impact, utility infrastructure requirements, and similar site-specific and use-specific needs assessments as necessary to prevent nuisance conditions and promote health, safety, and welfare.
(7) Electric supply.
(a) Prior to the city's approval of a land disturbance permit for a data center, the applicant shall submit to the city a letter from the electric power provider confirming capacity and willingness to serve the project, including any restrictions or limitations imposed by the power provider (e.g. mandatory load shed schedule, substation, etc.).
(b) The city may require a power impact study, phasing plans, and provision of a binding agreement between the data center's power provider and developer in order to ensure long-term service reliability.
(c) No primary onsite power generation shall be permitted.
(d) Substations are considered accessory uses to data centers.
(e) If the developer desires to utilize City of Griffin as the electrical provider, the developer will be required to enter an agreement whereby City of Griffin would provide power to the project. Any power agreement shall be separate and distinct from the development agreement contemplated by this section.
(f) With the exception of testing activities, generator use is limited to temporary or emergency backup use only. Use as prime power, rate curtailment, and storm avoidance shall not constitute a valid temporary or emergency backup use.
(g) The applicant must provide a utility inventory showing the power lines and infrastructure easements as part of the concept plan.
(h) Applicants shall provide, at a minimum, require the following plans and studies related to electrical supply, provided that the city may request other plans or studies as necessary to evaluate the impact on public health, safety, and welfare:
(i) Energy consumption & sustainability plan.
(ii) Lighting plan.
(iii) Transmission line impact assessment (required for major data center only).
(i) Additional electric supply regulations such as limitations on location of substations, setbacks, and burial of electric infrastructure, may be imposed as a condition of special use approval or as part of the required development agreement between the city and the applicant based on the specific use and site plan, environmental impact, utility infrastructure requirements, and similar site-specific and use-specific needs assessments as necessary to prevent nuisance conditions and promote health, safety, and welfare.
(8) Stormwater.
(a) A stormwater management plan shall be required, incorporating best management practices and designed to address runoff from large impervious surfaces associated with data center development.
(b) Stormwater management shall comply with all applicable City of Griffin standards, both during the land disturbance and construction phase and when operating as a data center, and incorporate best available and feasible practices, including green infrastructure and low impact development techniques, where practicable, to ensure post-development runoff meets or exceeds predevelopment conditions and minimizes downstream impacts.

(10) Decommissioning requirements for data centers.
(a) Decommissioning plan required. The owner or developer of a major data center must submit a decommissioning plan to the City of Griffin prior to issuance of a land disturbance permit. Said plan should be attached and/or incorporated into the development agreement.
(b) Plan contents. The following subjects, at a minimum, shall be considered in decommissioning plans for major data centers and shall, in the discretion of the city, be as detailed as necessary to ensure proper closure and post-closure impacts on the community and the environment are mitigated:
(i) Timeline: A detailed timeline for the decommissioning process, including key milestones and estimated completion dates for each phase of the decommissioning activities.
(ii) Equipment and material removal procedures: Specific procedures for the safe dismantling and removal of all equipment, materials, and structures from the data warehouse site. This should include methods for handling and transporting equipment to prevent damage and ensure safety.
(iii) Hazardous materials management: Detailed methods for identifying, handling, and disposing of hazardous materials in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations. This should include a list of all hazardous materials present on-site and the procedures for their safe removal and disposal.
(iv) Site remediation plan: A comprehensive plan for site remediation, including soil and groundwater testing, identification of any contamination, and proposed cleanup measures. This should also include a timeline for remediation activities and methods for monitoring and verifying the effectiveness of the remediation efforts.
(v) Site restoration plan: A detailed plan for restoring the site to a condition suitable for future use. This should include the removal of any remaining structures, re-vegetation, landscaping, and any other necessary measures to ensure the site is safe and aesthetically pleasing.
(vi) Health and safety measures: Procedures to ensure the health and safety of works and the surrounding community during the decommissioning process. This should include measures for dust control, noise reduction, and protection from hazardous materials.
(vii) Compliance and reporting: A plan for ensuring compliance with all applicable regulations and the approved decommissioning plan. This should include procedures for regular reporting to the City of Griffin, including progress reports and a final decommissioning report.
(c) Decommissioning compliance. Compliance during the decommissioning process will be monitored through the following methods to ensure that all activities adhere to the approved decommissioning plan and applicable regulations:
(i) Regular inspections: The City of Griffin will conduct regular inspections of the data center site. These inspections will verify that decommissioning activities are being carried out according to the approved plan and identify any deviations or non-compliance issues early on.
(ii) Progress reports: Developers or owners, as applicable, are required to submit quarterly progress reports detailing the decommissioning activities completed during the reporting period. These reports will include summaries of work done, any deviations from the plan, reasons for deviations, and updated timelines for remaining activities. This ensures continuous oversight and accountability.
(iii) Final report: Upon completion of the decommissioning process, Developers must submit a comprehensive final report. This report will include a detailed account of all decommissioning activities, documentation of equipment and hazardous materials removal, evidence of the site remediation and restoration, compliance certification, financial summary, and a community impact assessment.
(iv) Documentation and record-keeping: Records of all decommissioning activities, including records of equipment removal, hazardous materials disposal, site remediation efforts, and compliance with data protection regulations, must be maintained.
(v) Third-party audits: In some cases, third-party audits may be conducted to provide an independent assessment of the decommissioning process.
(d) Financial assurance.
(i) Decommissioning bond requirement: Developers must provide a decommissioning bond to cover the cost of decommission, removal, remediation, and mitigation of impacts remaining on the site. The bond amount shall be adequate to ensure the complete decommissioning of the data center and restoration of the site.
(ii) Bond amount determination: The amount of the decommissioning bond may be determined by the City of Griffin based on an estimate provided by a qualified independent engineer, and shall include:
(A) Costs for the removal of all equipment and materials
(B) Costs for the disposal of hazardous materials
(C) Costs for site remediation and mitigation, including soil and groundwater testing and cleanup, if necessary
(D) Costs for site restoration, including re-vegetation and any necessary landscaping
(iii) Bond review and adjustment: The bond amount shall be reviewed and may be adjusted periodically, as determined by the City of Griffin, to ensure it remains adequate to cover the decommissioning costs.
(iv) Form of financial assurance: The financial assurance may be provided in the form of a bond, escrow account, letter of credit, or other financial instrument deemed acceptable.

The purpose of this chapter is to regulate the placement of unattended donation boxes within incorporated areas of the city. The procedures and requirements of this chapter are intended to: promote the community's health, safety, and welfare by regulating unattended donation boxes for clothing or other salvageable personal property; ensure that unattended donation boxes do not pose a hazard to pedestrian and vehicular traffic; ensure that material is not allowed to accumulate outside of the unattended donation boxes where it can be scattered by adverse weather conditions, animal contacts and human activities; and establish criteria that avoid attracting vermin, unsightliness, and public health hazards.
1. As used in this section, the term "donation box" shall be defined as follows:
a. Donation box shall mean any unattended container, receptacle, or similar device used for soliciting and collecting donations of clothing and/or other salvageable personal property. This term does not include any unattended donation box location within a building which is permitted by-right.
b. All existing donation boxes erected on land within the city limits of Griffin, within 65 days of the effective date of this ordinance, shall register with the planning and development services department.
2. In addition to accessory uses otherwise permitted in this chapter, donation boxes may only be installed by obtaining a permit under the following conditions and requirements:
a. Application. Prior to delivery and/or installation of any donation box, an application shall be filed with the planning and zoning administrator or his/her designee identifying the size, color, and location of each donation box, as well as any signage proposed on the exterior of the donation box. A permit shall be required for each donation box installed within the city limits.
b. Zoning. Donation boxes shall only be permitted within the non-residential zoning districts, unless otherwise specified herein.
c. Approval of property owner. As a part of the application process, a letter must be provided from the owner of the property indicating they are aware and approve the installation of a donation box on their property, including that they are aware of their responsibility to maintain the current operator contact information and, if necessary, maintain or remove the donation box if the operator does not follow the provisions of this section.
d. Fees. Fees shall be $100.00 to be paid at the time of registration or application.
e. Size. Donation boxes shall be limited to no more than 128 cubic feet (i.e., four feet wide × four feet deep × eight feet tall). The height of each donation box shall not exceed eight feet in height from finish grade to the highest point of the roof.
f. Color. Donation boxes shall be painted or stained with a low reflectance and subtle, neutral or earth-tone color scheme. High-intensity colors, metallic colors, or fluorescent colors shall not be used.
g. Number of boxes permitted. Property equal to or less than one acre shall have a maximum of one donation box. Property greater than one acre shall allow one donation box per acre with a maximum of five boxes. When multiple donation boxes are located on an individual property, they must be adjacent to one another.
h. Location. Donation boxes shall be installed on a paved surface but may not be located within a designated parking space, drive aisle, or loading area. Donation boxes shall not be located within any building setback or established buffer area. Donation boxes shall not be located in such a manner that they block sight lines on the subject tract as determined by the city engineer. To the extent feasible, donation boxes shall be placed so as to be inconspicuous as viewed from the public right-of-way. Donation boxes are permitted only on properties where there is an active primary use and shall not be permitted on vacant lots or abandoned property.
i. Signage/contact information. The total square footage for all signage on each donation box shall not exceed two square feet. No advertising shall be permitted on the donation box. An additional sign shall contain the following contact information: the name, address, email, and phone number of both the property owner/manager and operator; it too shall not exceed two square feet.
j. Cleanliness of premises. Donation boxes shall be maintained in good condition and appearance with no structural damage, holes, or visible rust, and shall be free of graffiti.
(1) All donation boxes shall be free of debris and shall be serviced regularly so as to prevent overflow of donations or the accumulation of junk, debris or other material.
(2) Donated items or materials shall not remain or be allowed outside donation boxes and the area around each box. The owner or operator of the donation box, as well as the property owner of the parcel, shall be responsible for maintaining the area around each donation box so that it is free of litter, garbage and any other undesirable material.
k. Revocation of permit. Any permit granted pursuant to the provisions of this section may be subject to revocation for cause by the development services director (or his/her designee), including but not limited to, the failure to comply with this section or any other applicable provisions of the City's Code of Ordinances.
l. Renewal of permit. The term of the permit shall expire one year from the date of issuance. An operator may apply for permit renewal by submitting to the development services director before the expiration of the permit, a renewal application and associated fee.
(1) No person to whom a permit has been issued shall transfer, assign, or convey such permit to another person.
(2) Prior to expiration of the permit, the permittee may voluntarily cancel the permit by notifying the development services director in writing of the intent to cancel the permit. The permit shall become void upon the director's receipt of a written notice of intent to cancel the permit.
(3) Donation boxes shall be removed when the property becomes vacant or is foreclosed upon.
m. Approval/denial of permit. The development services director shall approve a new or renewal permit application if he/she finds that no circumstances exist at the time the application is reviewed, or existed at any time during which the previous permit was in effect, that are inconsistent with any requirement in this section.
n. Display of permit. The operator of the donation box and the property owner shall be responsible for maintaining the permit for each donation box required by this section. The development services director shall inspect each donation box following its installation to ensure the donation box is installed in accordance with the approved permit. Once it is determined the donation box complies with said permit, a decal shall be affixed to the actual donation box indicating the donation box has been approved. The purpose of this decal shall be to notify city officers and employees that the donation box complies with the provisions of this chapter and the approved donation box permit application.
o. Violations. Violations of this ordinance shall be punishable in the municipal court of the City of Griffin as an offense against the city. Violators shall be punished as provided in Section 1-12. Each and every day that any such violation exists shall be deemed a separate offense or violation.

133: A legal non-conforming structure may not be enlarged or extended unless a special use permit is issued in accordance with Section 406. A legal non-conforming structure may be maintained, repaired or structurally altered, under permit, in accordance with all pertinent building codes and ordinances. Failure to maintain a non-conforming structure in minimal compliance with applicable codes and ordinances, such that the general condition of the structure constitutes dilapidation or significant disrepair, shall create a rebuttable presumption of the owner or occupier's intent to abandon the non-conforming structure. Revocation of a structure's certificate of occupancy for a period in excess of one year shall also evidence the owner or occupier's intent to abandon the non-conforming structure.
134: A legal non-conforming use, in active existence on the effective date of this ordinance, may be continued without interference until such time as the property owner or occupier intentionally relinquishes his right to maintain such use, as evidenced by an overt act, or failure to act, sufficient to support a finding of such intent. For purposes of this ordinance, discontinuance of the use for a period of one year or more shall create a rebuttable presumption of the owner or occupier's intent to abandon the non-conforming use. A legal, non-conforming use may not be enlarged or expanded to a less restrictive use (i.e. residential to commercial) unless a special use permit is issued in accordance with Article 4 of this ordinance.
135: Discontinuance of a legal non-conforming use or structure following its destruction by fire or other natural hazard shall not evidence intent to abandon if the owner applies for a permit to rebuild the structure or otherwise reactivate the use, within six months of the occurrence; provided, however, this period may be extended for an additional six months, but not to exceed a total of one year from the date of the occurrence, if the owner demonstrates substantial progress, time, effort and money in renovation of the structure.

137: Where the zoning administrator determines a use or structure was rendered non-conforming by the adoption of this ordinance or any amendment thereto, he or she shall notify the property owner, in writing, that the use or structure constitutes a legal non-conforming use or legal non-conforming structure and inform the owner of the consequences of the abandonment of such use or structure under the provisions of this ordinance. An owner may appeal the determination of the zoning administrator to the board of commissioners.
138: Notwithstanding any other provision of this ordinance, any existing non-conforming use or structure which was illegal under any prior zoning ordinance shall continue to be an illegal non-conforming use or structure under this ordinance unless the use or structure is expressly permitted by this ordinance and meets all criteria for a permitted use or structure within its assigned zoning classification.
